_comment: Every threshold the feature extractor uses. No defaults live in the code. Every key must have an entry in _provenance; extract_features.py refuses to run otherwise. Under the organisers' 2026-11-03 rules nothing may be tuned on the ground truth or the video: a value is either published, follows from the Laws of the Game or physics, or is an a-priori choice to be tuned on EXTERNAL data only (tuned_on names the dataset once that happens).

fps.source: games.py GAMES['BAR-ATH']['fps'] and DATA.md; the script asserts the two agree
fps.reason: Frame rate of the tactical video and its ATD.

kickoff_video_frames.reason: First-half kickoff is the first graded frame; second-half kickoff is 113742 (the 2nd half is graded from 110808, so 2,934 frames before it are dead ball).

kickoff_window_frames.source: IFAB Laws of the Game, Law 8 (The Start and Restart of Play)
kickoff_window_frames.reason: At a kickoff every player must be in their own half. Averaging positions over the 26 rows (k-25..k or k..k+25, about 1 s) next to the kickoff (side: kickoff_window_side) reads each team's side robustly against single-frame tracking noise. Used only to find attacking direction.

kickoff_window_side.source: data format: BAR-ATH tracking runs before each kickoff; IDSSE positions start at (or just before) each kickoff, so idsse_features.py takes the first alive row (DFL BallStatus) of each period as the kickoff and asserts the resulting signs agree with kloppy's orientation
kickoff_window_side.reason: Which side of the kickoff the attack-direction window sits on. BAR-ATH tracking runs before each kickoff, so the 1 s before it is used, when every player is in their own half by law. On IDSSE the rows before a period's first alive row are either the other period or dead pre-kickoff rows with no guaranteed formation, so the 1 s after the first alive row is used instead. In 1 s a centroid moves at most a few metres, far less than the half-pitch separation, and the 5 m separation assert still guards the result.

kickoff_min_centroid_separation_m.source: IFAB Laws of the Game, Law 8
kickoff_min_centroid_separation_m.reason: With both teams in their own halves, their centroids are separated along the pitch length by a large margin. 5 m is a deliberately loose lower bound used only in an assertion, so a wrong axis orientation or kickoff frame makes the script stop instead of producing mirrored features. Not a modelling threshold.

ball_max_interp_gap_frames.reason: Linear interpolation assumes no touch inside the gap. Limiting it to 0.48 s (12 frames) keeps that assumption plausible while bridging short occlusions; longer gaps stay NaN so later stages can treat them as unknown.
ball_max_interp_gap_frames.revisit: tune on external matches with artificially dropped ball frames

velocity_half_window_frames.reason: Central difference over +/-2 frames (0.16 s total) balances noise against time resolution. Possession boundaries must be placed within a few frames, so wider windows would smear touches.

turn_min_speed_m_s.reason: Below about 1 m/s the ball's displacement over the velocity window (4 cm) is comparable to tracking jitter, so its direction is meaningless and the turn angle is set to NaN.
turn_min_speed_m_s.revisit: check against jitter measured on external tracking

ball_still_speed_m_s.source: IFAB Laws of the Game, Laws 8, 13, 14, 16, 17 (ball must be stationary at kickoffs, free kicks, penalties, goal kicks, corners)
ball_still_speed_m_s.reason: Restarts are taken from a stationary ball. 0.5 m/s is the 'stationary' cut-off, leaving room for tracking jitter.

ball_still_half_window_frames.reason: Stillness is measured over +/-0.48 s so a single slow frame in open play (a ball at the top of a bounce, a trap) does not look like a placed ball.

player_max_plausible_speed_m_s.source: human sprint record about 12.4 m/s (Bolt, 100 m, 2009); elite footballers top out around 10 m/s
player_max_plausible_speed_m_s.reason: A per-track velocity above any human's is a tracker identity switch, not running. Set just above the human record so no real sprint is dropped.

player_walking_speed_m_s.source: conventional football speed-zone boundary of 7.2 km/h between walking and jogging (e.g. Bradley et al. 2009, J Sports Sci)
player_walking_speed_m_s.reason: Share of players walking is a dead-ball cue: play stops and players slow down.

near_ball_radii_m.source: 3 m: design choice (about one stride plus reach); 10 m: IFAB Laws 8, 13, 17 require opponents at least 9.15 m from the ball at kickoffs, free kicks and corners
near_ball_radii_m.reason: Counts of players within playing distance (3 m) and within the restart exclusion distance (10 m, just above 9.15 m) of the ball.
near_ball_radii_m.revisit: 3 m radius: tune on external matches

speed_unit_check_moving_m_s.source: design choice; same value as MOVING_MPS in features/external/fetch_idsse.py
speed_unit_check_moving_m_s.reason: Report-only check of the raw player speed field's unit: only player-frames whose position speed exceeds 2 m/s are used, well above position noise (a few cm per frame at 25 fps), so the ratio is not dominated by jitter on standing players. Affects no feature.

speed_unit_check_tolerance.source: design choice; same value as SPEED_RATIO_TOL in features/external/fetch_idsse.py
speed_unit_check_tolerance.reason: Report-only: the ratio is called m/s if within 10% of 1, km/h if within 10% of 3.6, else unknown. Only prints an interpretation line; nothing is asserted or converted.

smart_tagging_team_map.source: DATA.md Smart Tagging table: Team values are 'Barcelona', 'Atletic Club' (sic) and 'N/A'
smart_tagging_team_map.reason: Maps tag teams to the submission's H/A. N/A is kept as its own value (DATA.md: every throw-in is tagged N/A), never folded into a team.

ball_loss_dead_drop_prob.reason: Ball-loss simulation on IDSSE only (features/external/degrade_ball.py). Probability that a DFL dead span whose gap is >= 126 frames (5 s) loses the ball: 1.0. User's decision: a tactical-camera ball tracker is assumed to lose the ball whenever it is dead for 5 s or more (a player holds it, it is off the pitch, or out of shot). Chosen without fitting; but the authors had already seen BAR-ATH's label-free tracking aggregates (docs/findings.md) and the earlier BAR-ATH-fitted values (features/external/ball_loss_fitted_bar_ath.json), so the choice is not blind. Fixed 2026-11-15 before rebuilding the degraded tables and not revised after seeing them.

ball_loss_short_gap_drop_prob.reason: Ball-loss simulation on IDSSE only (features/external/degrade_ball.py). Probability that a dead span whose gap is 1-125 frames (under 5 s) loses the ball: 0.5. There is no prior knowledge whether a brief stoppage loses the ball, so the maximum-ignorance value. Chosen without fitting; but the authors had already seen BAR-ATH's label-free tracking aggregates (docs/findings.md) and the earlier BAR-ATH-fitted values (features/external/ball_loss_fitted_bar_ath.json), so the choice is not blind. Fixed 2026-11-15 before rebuilding the degraded tables and not revised after seeing them.

ball_loss_onset_lag_frames.reason: Ball-loss simulation on IDSSE only (features/external/degrade_ball.py). A dropped dead span starts this many frames after DFL marks the ball dead, drawn per span uniform on [0, 100] inclusive (0-4 s) from the per-(match, seed) RNG. The tracker keeps following the ball for a moment after it goes dead (rolling out, being collected). User's a priori choice (2026-11-15, replacing the fixed 50), made to stop the simulator fixing dead-ball edges exactly: with a fixed lag the ball vanished exactly 50 frames after every DFL dead onset. Not fitted to anything. The spread was fixed before the degraded tables were rebuilt and not revised after seeing them. Even a span dropped with probability 1.0 now has random edges. The spread itself is an assumption; the authors had already seen BAR-ATH's label-free tracking aggregates (docs/findings.md) and the earlier fitted values, so it is not blind. Timing: decided after the fixed-lag tune and held-out harness runs, motivated by the fixed-edge leak the reviewer found in the simulator's structure, not by any score.

ball_loss_reacquisition_lag_frames.reason: Ball-loss simulation on IDSSE only (features/external/degrade_ball.py). A dropped dead span ends at the restart (first DFL alive row) plus this lag, drawn per span uniform on [0, 25] inclusive (0-1 s) from the per-(match, seed) RNG, and clipped to the period end. Not identifiable from any data we may use (docs/findings.md sensitivity). User's a priori choice (2026-11-15, replacing the fixed 0), made to stop the simulator fixing dead-ball edges exactly: with lag 0 the ball reappeared on exactly the DFL restart frame. Not fitted to anything. The spread was fixed before the degraded tables were rebuilt and not revised after seeing them. Even a span dropped with probability 1.0 now has random edges. The spread itself is an assumption; the authors had already seen BAR-ATH's label-free tracking aggregates (docs/findings.md) and the earlier fitted values, so it is not blind. Timing: decided after the fixed-lag tune and held-out harness runs, motivated by the fixed-edge leak the reviewer found in the simulator's structure, not by any score.

ball_loss_live_gaps_per_hour.reason: Ball-loss simulation on IDSSE only (features/external/degrade_ball.py). Poisson rate of long ball losses inside live play, per hour of period: 30 (occlusion in crowds, aerial balls). Deliberately nonzero so that on degraded IDSSE 'ball missing' is not a proxy for 'dead' and a dead-ball detector must use player cues. A round guess. Chosen without fitting; but the authors had already seen BAR-ATH's label-free tracking aggregates (docs/findings.md) and the earlier BAR-ATH-fitted values (features/external/ball_loss_fitted_bar_ath.json), so the choice is not blind. Fixed 2026-11-15 before rebuilding the degraded tables and not revised after seeing them.

ball_loss_live_gap_frames_range.reason: Ball-loss simulation on IDSSE only (features/external/degrade_ball.py). Live-play loss length, log-uniform between these frame counts: [126, 500] (5-20 s; 126 is the long-gap edge). Same reasoning as ball_loss_live_gaps_per_hour; a round guess. Chosen without fitting; but the authors had already seen BAR-ATH's label-free tracking aggregates (docs/findings.md) and the earlier BAR-ATH-fitted values (features/external/ball_loss_fitted_bar_ath.json), so the choice is not blind. Fixed 2026-11-15 before rebuilding the degraded tables and not revised after seeing them.

ball_loss_flickers_per_hour.reason: Ball-loss simulation on IDSSE only (features/external/degrade_ball.py). Poisson rate of brief detector dropouts in live play, per hour of period: 10. A round guess. Chosen without fitting; but the authors had already seen BAR-ATH's label-free tracking aggregates (docs/findings.md) and the earlier BAR-ATH-fitted values (features/external/ball_loss_fitted_bar_ath.json), so the choice is not blind. Fixed 2026-11-15 before rebuilding the degraded tables and not revised after seeing them.

ball_loss_flicker_frames_range.reason: Ball-loss simulation on IDSSE only (features/external/degrade_ball.py). Flicker length, uniform on these frame counts inclusive: [1, 12] (up to about half a second, the extractor's ball interpolation limit). A round guess. Chosen without fitting; but the authors had already seen BAR-ATH's label-free tracking aggregates (docs/findings.md) and the earlier BAR-ATH-fitted values (features/external/ball_loss_fitted_bar_ath.json), so the choice is not blind. Fixed 2026-11-15 before rebuilding the degraded tables and not revised after seeing them.

dead_out_margin_m.source: dead-ball detector v1 (features/dead_ball.py, docs/dead-ball-detector-design.md); main-session/user instruction 2026-11-15
dead_out_margin_m.reason: Law 9: the ball is out when the whole ball has crossed the line, i.e. its centre is more than its radius (0.11 m, Law 2 circumference 68-70 cm) beyond the line. Plus 0.5 m allowed for ball tracking error (an assumption, stated a priori: a tactical-camera ball position is taken to be good to about half a metre), so a ball on the line is not called out by jitter.
dead_out_margin_m.revisit: check the tracking-error part on IDSSE (design section 5); not graded by score

dead_placed_still_frac_min.source: dead-ball detector v1 (features/dead_ball.py, docs/dead-ball-detector-design.md); main-session/user instruction 2026-11-15
dead_placed_still_frac_min.reason: Placed-ball candidate: ball_still_frac (share of still frames over the symmetric +/-ball_still_half_window_frames window) at least this, with the players stopped. A majority threshold on a symmetric window puts the candidate's edges at the frame where the ball starts or stops moving, so the restart (end) is not shifted by the window.

dead_vanish_offset_frames.source: dead-ball detector v1 (features/dead_ball.py, docs/dead-ball-detector-design.md); main-session/user instruction 2026-11-15
dead_vanish_offset_frames.reason: Start of a D gap when neither a line crossing nor a deceleration onset is available: the ball-vanish frame plus this offset. 0: the tracker loses the ball when play stops. Never tuned: on degraded IDSSE the vanish edge is set by the simulator's onset-lag assumption, so tuning it would fit that assumption (user decision 2026-11-15).

dead_reappear_offset_frames.source: dead-ball detector v1 (features/dead_ball.py, docs/dead-ball-detector-design.md); main-session/user instruction 2026-11-15
dead_reappear_offset_frames.reason: End of a D gap = the first frame the ball is seen again plus this offset (reacquisition lag 0: reappearance = the restart, findings 2026-11-09). Cannot be measured externally (design section 3). Never tuned: on degraded IDSSE the reappear edge is set by the simulator's reacquisition-lag assumption (user decision 2026-11-15).

dead_decel_lag_frames.source: dead-ball detector v1 (features/dead_ball.py, docs/dead-ball-detector-design.md); main-session/user instruction 2026-11-15
dead_decel_lag_frames.reason: A priori: Whistle -> deceleration lag. A D gap's start = onset of the stopped run (smoothed speed and walking past their thresholds) minus this lag. 1 s: about 0.2-0.3 s auditory reaction plus the time for the mean speed of 20 players to fall to walking pace. First-principles guess (a priori value 25). Tuned value 0 (2026-11-16: full joint grid over dead_ball.TUNABLE (15000 combos; this key over [0, 12, 25, 50, 75]), objective: maximise mean spell_f1_mean over the 15 degraded runs (5 tuning matches x seeds [0, 1, 2]), harness.run -> pm.evaluate; tie rule: among combos within 0.002 of the best mean spell_f1_mean, pick the highest mean alive_dead_f1; if still tied (equal to 1e-12), the one closest to the a priori values (sum over keys of |grid index - a priori grid index|), then the first in grid order. Chosen 0. On the edge of its grid (see docs/findings.md, dead-ball detector tuning)).
dead_decel_lag_frames.tuned_on: IDSSE J03WMX, J03WN1, J03WOH, J03WOY, J03WQQ (degraded a priori ball-loss, seeds 0-2); held out J03WPY, J03WR9
dead_decel_lag_frames.target: IDSSE DFL BallStatus/BallPossession proxy labels, spell_f1_mean via evaluation/possession_metrics.py. Never BAR-ATH GT or video.

dead_smooth_half_window_frames.source: dead-ball detector v1 (features/dead_ball.py, docs/dead-ball-detector-design.md); main-session/user instruction 2026-11-15
dead_smooth_half_window_frames.reason: A priori: Change-point / smoothing window: walking share and mean speed are averaged over +/-12 frames (about 1 s, same as ball_still_half_window_frames) inside the half block, so single-frame tracking noise neither starts nor breaks a stopped run (a priori value 12). Tuned value 0 (2026-11-16: full joint grid over dead_ball.TUNABLE (15000 combos; this key over [0, 3, 6, 12, 18, 25]), objective: maximise mean spell_f1_mean over the 15 degraded runs (5 tuning matches x seeds [0, 1, 2]), harness.run -> pm.evaluate; tie rule: among combos within 0.002 of the best mean spell_f1_mean, pick the highest mean alive_dead_f1; if still tied (equal to 1e-12), the one closest to the a priori values (sum over keys of |grid index - a priori grid index|), then the first in grid order. Chosen 0. On the edge of its grid (see docs/findings.md, dead-ball detector tuning)).
dead_smooth_half_window_frames.tuned_on: IDSSE J03WMX, J03WN1, J03WOH, J03WOY, J03WQQ (degraded a priori ball-loss, seeds 0-2); held out J03WPY, J03WR9
dead_smooth_half_window_frames.target: IDSSE DFL BallStatus/BallPossession proxy labels, spell_f1_mean via evaluation/possession_metrics.py. Never BAR-ATH GT or video.

dead_walking_frac_min.source: dead-ball detector v1 (features/dead_ball.py, docs/dead-ball-detector-design.md); main-session/user instruction 2026-11-15
dead_walking_frac_min.reason: A priori: Players stopped: smoothed share of players walking (min of the two teams; all_walking_frac where a team's share is NaN) at least 0.8, i.e. all but about 4 of 22 walking (a keeper or a set-piece taker may still jog). A first-principles value; not blind: the BAR-ATH label-free gap aggregates (median 0.95 in long gaps vs 0.62 with the ball seen, docs/findings.md) had been seen (a priori value 0.8). Tuned value 0.7 (2026-11-16: full joint grid over dead_ball.TUNABLE (15000 combos; this key over [0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 0.95]), objective: maximise mean spell_f1_mean over the 15 degraded runs (5 tuning matches x seeds [0, 1, 2]), harness.run -> pm.evaluate; tie rule: among combos within 0.002 of the best mean spell_f1_mean, pick the highest mean alive_dead_f1; if still tied (equal to 1e-12), the one closest to the a priori values (sum over keys of |grid index - a priori grid index|), then the first in grid order. Chosen 0.7).
dead_walking_frac_min.tuned_on: IDSSE J03WMX, J03WN1, J03WOH, J03WOY, J03WQQ (degraded a priori ball-loss, seeds 0-2); held out J03WPY, J03WR9
dead_walking_frac_min.target: IDSSE DFL BallStatus/BallPossession proxy labels, spell_f1_mean via evaluation/possession_metrics.py. Never BAR-ATH GT or video.

dead_mean_speed_max_m_s.source: dead-ball detector v1 (features/dead_ball.py, docs/dead-ball-detector-design.md); main-session/user instruction 2026-11-15
dead_mean_speed_max_m_s.reason: A priori: Players stopped: smoothed all_mean_speed at most 1.5 m/s, about ordinary human walking pace (~1.4 m/s, e.g. Bohannon 1997, Age Ageing) and below the 2.0 m/s walking/jogging zone boundary. Not blind: the BAR-ATH label-free aggregates (median 1.00 m/s in gaps vs 1.93 seen) had been seen (a priori value 1.5). Tuned value 2.0 (2026-11-16: full joint grid over dead_ball.TUNABLE (15000 combos; this key over [1.0, 1.25, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5]), objective: maximise mean spell_f1_mean over the 15 degraded runs (5 tuning matches x seeds [0, 1, 2]), harness.run -> pm.evaluate; tie rule: among combos within 0.002 of the best mean spell_f1_mean, pick the highest mean alive_dead_f1; if still tied (equal to 1e-12), the one closest to the a priori values (sum over keys of |grid index - a priori grid index|), then the first in grid order. Chosen 2.0).
dead_mean_speed_max_m_s.tuned_on: IDSSE J03WMX, J03WN1, J03WOH, J03WOY, J03WQQ (degraded a priori ball-loss, seeds 0-2); held out J03WPY, J03WR9
dead_mean_speed_max_m_s.target: IDSSE DFL BallStatus/BallPossession proxy labels, spell_f1_mean via evaluation/possession_metrics.py. Never BAR-ATH GT or video.

dead_min_gap_frames.source: dead-ball detector v1 (features/dead_ball.py, docs/dead-ball-detector-design.md); main-session/user instruction 2026-11-15
dead_min_gap_frames.reason: A ball-unknown run is a D candidate (a) only if at least 50 frames (2 s) long: a stoppage and restart (fetch, place, take) takes at least about 2 s, and 50 is well above the 12-frame interpolation limit so dropouts in play are not candidates. A priori value 50. Tuned 2026-11-16: full joint grid over dead_ball.TUNABLE (15000 combos; this key over [25, 50, 100, 150]), objective: maximise mean spell_f1_mean over the 15 degraded runs (5 tuning matches x seeds [0, 1, 2]), harness.run -> pm.evaluate; tie rule: among combos within 0.002 of the best mean spell_f1_mean, pick the highest mean alive_dead_f1; if still tied (equal to 1e-12), the one closest to the a priori values (sum over keys of |grid index - a priori grid index|), then the first in grid order. Chosen 50.
dead_min_gap_frames.tuned_on: IDSSE J03WMX, J03WN1, J03WOH, J03WOY, J03WQQ (degraded a priori ball-loss, seeds 0-2); held out J03WPY, J03WR9
dead_min_gap_frames.target: IDSSE DFL BallStatus/BallPossession proxy labels, spell_f1_mean via evaluation/possession_metrics.py. Never BAR-ATH GT or video.

dead_min_alive_frames.source: dead-ball detector v1 (features/dead_ball.py, docs/dead-ball-detector-design.md); main-session/user instruction 2026-11-15
dead_min_alive_frames.reason: Two D candidates separated by an alive run shorter than 25 frames (1 s), inside one half block, are merged: a restart followed by another stoppage within 1 s is implausible, and a spurious alive blip costs extra spells under spellF1. A priori value 25. Tuned 2026-11-16: full joint grid over dead_ball.TUNABLE (15000 combos; this key over [0, 12, 25, 50, 75]), objective: maximise mean spell_f1_mean over the 15 degraded runs (5 tuning matches x seeds [0, 1, 2]), harness.run -> pm.evaluate; tie rule: among combos within 0.002 of the best mean spell_f1_mean, pick the highest mean alive_dead_f1; if still tied (equal to 1e-12), the one closest to the a priori values (sum over keys of |grid index - a priori grid index|), then the first in grid order. Chosen 25.
dead_min_alive_frames.tuned_on: IDSSE J03WMX, J03WN1, J03WOH, J03WOY, J03WQQ (degraded a priori ball-loss, seeds 0-2); held out J03WPY, J03WR9
dead_min_alive_frames.target: IDSSE DFL BallStatus/BallPossession proxy labels, spell_f1_mean via evaluation/possession_metrics.py. Never BAR-ATH GT or video.

dead_min_dead_frames.reason: After candidate merging, every predicted D segment shorter than this many frames becomes alive (0 = off); segments holding a ctx known_dead frame are never dropped. Tuned 2026-11-16 by a one-key search (tune_dead_ball.py --tune-one) over [0, 12, 25, 38, 50] frames with every other dead_* key held at its config value; objective: maximise mean spell_f1_mean over the 15 degraded runs (5 tuning matches x seeds [0, 1, 2]), harness.run -> pm.evaluate; tie rule (declared before the run): highest mean spell_f1_mean; if the top values are within 0.001 of each other, take the smallest value among them. All five values lay within 0.001 of the best (25: 0.1222; 0: 0.1212), so 0 (off) was chosen. Clean tuning tables scored as a cross-check only, not used for selection. Not blind: the key was proposed after the 2026-11-16 held-out D-segment count look (16.8-18.8% of predicted held-out segments under 1 s) and the label-free BAR-ATH report (13 of 145 under 1 s) had been seen; the user decided the grid and the tuning-only objective. With 0 chosen the detector is identical to the version scored on held-out. The joint dead_* grid (tune_log.json) ran before this key existed, i.e. with it effectively 0.
dead_min_dead_frames.tuned_on: IDSSE J03WMX, J03WN1, J03WOH, J03WOY, J03WQQ (degraded a priori ball-loss, seeds 0-2); held out J03WPY, J03WR9
dead_min_dead_frames.target: IDSSE DFL BallStatus/BallPossession proxy labels, spell_f1_mean via evaluation/possession_metrics.py. Never BAR-ATH GT or video.

dead_onset_max_lookback_frames.reason: Bounds the backward search for the deceleration onset: the stopped run containing the ball-vanish frame may reach back at most 125 frames (5 s). If it starts earlier, the D start is clipped to vanish - 125, with no lag applied. A referee whistles within seconds of play stopping, so a longer slow stretch with the ball still tracked is live play, not a stoppage. Not tuned.

decoder_margin_full_m.reason: Per-frame team score = clip(nearest_margin_m / this, -1, 1): +1 = home clearly closer, -1 = away. 2 m (about one stride) is where being closer stops being ambiguous: within it, a challenge or tracking error can swap the nearest player; beyond it, the closer team can play the ball first. Below the 3 m near-ball radius. Set before any decoder run. A priori value 2.0. Tuned value 1.0 (2026-11-16: full grid over the six decoder_* keys, 729 combos; this key over [1.0, 2.0, 4.0]; objective: maximise mean spell_f1_mean over the 15 degraded runs (5 tuning matches x seeds [0, 1, 2]), harness.run -> pm.evaluate, with the dead_* values frozen; tie rule: among combos within 0.002 of the best mean spell_f1_mean, the one closest to the a priori values (sum over keys of |grid index - a priori grid index|), then the first in grid order). Chosen 1.0.
decoder_margin_full_m.tuned_on: IDSSE J03WMX, J03WN1, J03WOH, J03WOY, J03WQQ (degraded a priori ball-loss, seeds 0-2); held out J03WPY, J03WR9
decoder_margin_full_m.target: IDSSE DFL BallStatus/BallPossession proxy labels, spell_f1_mean via evaluation/possession_metrics.py. Never BAR-ATH GT or video.

decoder_c_score.reason: Per-frame score of the contested/loose state C where both teams, or neither, have a player within 3 m (a duel, or the ball in flight). 1.0 = as strong as a clear (>= 2 m margin) team frame: a duel or a ball in flight is as clear a sign that nobody controls it. Elsewhere C scores 0. C never splits a spell (its frames take the preceding team's label). Set before any decoder run. A priori value 1.0. Tuned value 0.5 (2026-11-16: full grid over the six decoder_* keys, 729 combos; this key over [0.0, 0.5, 1.0]; objective: maximise mean spell_f1_mean over the 15 degraded runs (5 tuning matches x seeds [0, 1, 2]), harness.run -> pm.evaluate, with the dead_* values frozen; tie rule: among combos within 0.002 of the best mean spell_f1_mean, the one closest to the a priori values (sum over keys of |grid index - a priori grid index|), then the first in grid order). Chosen 0.5.
decoder_c_score.tuned_on: IDSSE J03WMX, J03WN1, J03WOH, J03WOY, J03WQQ (degraded a priori ball-loss, seeds 0-2); held out J03WPY, J03WR9
decoder_c_score.target: IDSSE DFL BallStatus/BallPossession proxy labels, spell_f1_mean via evaluation/possession_metrics.py. Never BAR-ATH GT or video.

decoder_switch_penalty.reason: Viterbi cost of a direct H<->A switch, in per-frame score units. A clearly contrary frame costs 2 (from +1 to -1), so 50 = a switch needs about 1 s (25 frames) of clear contrary evidence: about a pass's flight time, so a ball passing near opponents does not flip possession, yet an order of magnitude below a typical possession of 10-15 s, so real changes still switch. The plain HMM rule log(spell length in frames) = log(300) ~ 6 would be far too small here: the per-frame scores are strongly autocorrelated, so a few frames of noise would switch. Set before any decoder run. A priori value 50.0.
